partner_context.their_ambition: Through your Ministry of Transport you are building a modern, multimodal network under the Comprehensive Transport Plan — and water is explicitly part of it. Your Water Taxi project has already delivered first-phase terminals at Lusail, The Pearl and the Corniche, with eco-friendly waterborne transport as a stated goal. Katara and Qatar Tourism, both prior Navier contacts, own your experience and destination layer.
partner_context.their_pressure: Doha's growth is concentrated on a compact, traffic-dense bay — West Bay, Lusail, The Pearl, Katara — where the fastest line between two points is across the water, not around it. You want a flagship, sustainable, world-class system befitting your post-2022 ambitions.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the premium, zero-emission, software-defined edge of the water network you are already building — turning your new water-taxi infrastructure into a fast, smooth, foiling system from day one.

hero.title: Qatar × Navier — the foiling water network for Doha Bay
hero.subtitle: Qatar is already building the water-taxi infrastructure. Navier makes it fly.
hero.what_we_do_together: We bring software-defined foiling vessels to Qatar's new water-taxi network — a premium, zero-emission system across Doha Bay's most congested and most iconic corridors. The Ministry of Transport brings the terminals, the mandate and the network; Katara and Qatar Tourism bring the destinations; Navier brings the fleet and the playbook proven in the Maldives.

why_now: The MOT has completed phase-one water-taxi infrastructure — Lusail Ferry Terminal plus Pearl and Corniche stops — and is explicit about eco-friendly waterborne transport. The terminals are going in; the question is what runs on them. A ~100-vessel Navier network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026). This is the moment to specify foiling as the standard.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the MOT's Comprehensive Transport Plan as the marine mode — integrated with the Doha Metro, tram and bus network, sharing the new water-taxi terminals, and tying the airport, the Corniche and the islands into one journey.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for Qatar?
objections.response: The entire Doha Bay network — West Bay, Lusail, The Pearl, Banana Island, the airport waterfront — sits within a few nautical miles, deep inside Pioneer II all-electric range. Quanta-LR covers any cross-Gulf ambition with no charging infrastructure.
Climate-controlled cabins, dramatically lower energy per mile, and scheduling flexibility around peak summer — the same as every Gulf mobility mode.
Software-defined controls, a clear first-of-class path, and an operating record in the US and the Maldives.

close.title: Qatar built the terminals. Navier makes the network fly.
close.body: The bay core proves it; the airport, the islands and the coast complete it — a flagship, zero-emission foiling network for Doha, integrated into the transport plan Qatar is already building.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is Qatar's coast as a connected water grid: Pearl-to-Lusail in minutes, the resort islands on demand, and a foiling link across the Gulf to Bahrain — convened top-down by MOTC.

deck_only.differentiation_vs_status_quo: Conventional water taxis are slow and diesel. Foiling vessels are fast, near-silent and zero-emission — a flagship-grade ride for a flagship destination.
